passages.title: Counting the world's languages
passages.body:
Directions: Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow, based solely on the passage.

An attempt to determine the number of languages in the world is affected by other factors. A few new languages do continue to be discovered, even these days, as unexplored regions of the world begin to be opened up. The discovery does not usually take place straight away. Often there are similarities with an already known language which make the investigators assume that what they have found is just a dialect of that language. Only after a considerable period of contact does it transpire that the speech is so different that it has to be considered a different language. It takes a language survey to establish the facts, and there are still many countries where such surveys are incomplete or have not even begun. The people may be known, but the identity of their language may not be. Because many such peoples are bilingual or multilingual, and converse with outsiders in lingua franca, it may take a while before linguists come to realize that there is an ethnic language there at all.
passages.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part A English

Which one of the following is NOT the reason for the difficulty in estimating the number of languages of the world?
questions.opt_a: New languages continue to be discovered

questions.topic: Active and Passive Voice / Direct and Indirect Speech
questions.theme: Reported statement with time and place shift
questions.question:
Directions: The item has a sentence in direct or indirect speech with four options. One of the options converts it correctly. Select the correct option.

Convert from direct speech to indirect speech:

Charu said to her friend, "I want you to be here at 6.00 p.m. tomorrow for the meeting."
questions.opt_a: Charu told her friend that she wanted her to be there at 6.00 p.m. the next day for the meeting
questions.opt_b: Charu told her friend that she wanted her to be there at 6.00 p.m. tomorrow for the meeting
questions.opt_c: Charu requested her friend that she wanted her to be there at 6.00 p.m. tomorrow for the meeting
questions.opt_d: Charu told her friend that she will want her to be here at 6.00 p.m. the next day for the meeting
questions.explanation:
'want' becomes 'wanted', 'here' becomes 'there' and 'tomorrow' becomes 'the next day'.
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part A English

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.topic: Active and Passive Voice / Direct and Indirect Speech
questions.question:
Directions: The item has a sentence in direct or indirect speech with four options. One of the options converts it correctly. Select the correct option.

Convert from direct speech to indirect speech:

Nitin said to his brother, "What a beautiful painting it is?"
questions.opt_a: Nitin wondered to his brother that what a beautiful painting it was
questions.opt_b: Nitin wondered before his brother that it was a beautiful painting
questions.opt_c: Nitin exclaimed that it is a beautiful painting
questions.opt_d: Nitin asked his brother whether it was beautiful painting
questions.explanation:
The sentence is an exclamation of wonder, so the reporting verb should express it, and 'is' must shift to 'was'. (c) keeps 'is' and (d) wrongly turns it into a question. (a) keeps the sense of wonder with the correct tense, though the usual form would be 'exclaimed that it was a very beautiful painting'.
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part A English

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.topic: Active and Passive Voice / Direct and Indirect Speech
questions.question:
Directions: The item has a sentence in indirect speech. Select the option that converts it correctly into direct speech.

The teacher asked her students why they had been quiet in the previous class.
questions.opt_a: The teacher asked her students, "Why were they keeping quiet in the previous class?"
questions.opt_b: The teacher said to her students, "Why were you quiet in the previous class?"
questions.opt_c: The teacher said to her students, "Why had you been quiet in the previous class?"
questions.opt_d: The teacher said to her students, "Why were you quiet in previous class?"
questions.explanation:
In direct speech the past perfect 'had been' goes back to the simple past 'were', 'they' becomes 'you', and 'the previous class' keeps its article.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part A English

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: The item consists of six sentences of a passage. The first and sixth sentences are given as S1 and S6. The middle four sentences have been jumbled and labelled P, Q, R and S. Find the proper sequence of the four sentences.

S1: Although all sources of energy ultimately come from natural processes, non-renewable resources cannot be replaced naturally at the rate they are being used.
S6: The sustainable use of natural resources in a manner that provides the maximum benefit of these resources to humans over a period of time can be termed as conservation.
P: This will increase the time and cost of mining and once these resources are used up they cannot be replaced.
Q: Hence, we must remember that though our country is rich in mineral deposits these resources are short-lived.
R: Extraction of these ores through the process of mining will soon become difficult and very expensive because these minerals have to be mined from greater depths over time.
S: Mineral resources can be said to be finite and non-renewable.
questions.explanation:
S states that minerals are finite; Q ('Hence ... short-lived') draws the consequence; R explains that extraction becomes harder; P ('This will increase the time and cost') follows from R and leads to conservation in S6.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part A English

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: The item consists of six sentences of a passage. The first and sixth sentences are given as S1 and S6. The middle four sentences have been jumbled and labelled P, Q, R and S. Find the proper sequence of the four sentences.

S1: India, at present, has one of the largest road networks in the world.
S6: It passes through Howrah, Delhi and Amritsar and terminates in Kabul (Afghanistan).
P: The importance of roads has been recognised in India since the ancient times.
Q: The Grand Trunk Road was built by Sher Shah Suri across the Indo-Gangetic plain, from Chittagong (Bangladesh) to Peshawar (Pakistan).
R: Kings such as Ashoka and Chandragupta built roads for easy transportation of goods and people.
S: Construction of roads continued as an important activity in the late medieval period.
questions.explanation:
The passage moves through time: ancient importance (P), Ashoka and Chandragupta (R), late medieval road building (S), and the Grand Trunk Road (Q), whose route continues in S6.
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part A English

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: The item consists of six sentences of a passage. The first and sixth sentences are given as S1 and S6. The middle four sentences have been jumbled and labelled P, Q, R and S. Find the proper sequence of the four sentences.

S1: National highways connect one state with another and are of national importance.
S6: These road systems are also known as primary road systems and are laid and operated under the supervision of the National Highway Authority of India.
P: They are important because whereas they constitute merely two per cent of the total road networks, they nevertheless carry 40 per cent of the total road traffic.
Q: The road infrastructure of the country is therefore crucial, and their construction and maintenance is of critical importance.
R: They bear the load of traffic because these roads connect long distances and pass through major cities and towns.
S: Since they cover the length and breadth of the nation and connect cities and towns, these highways are the primary facilitators of trade and connectivity.
questions.explanation:
P gives the 2%/40% fact; R explains why they carry so much traffic; S adds their role in trade; Q concludes ('therefore crucial'), before S6.
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part A English

Directions: The item consists of six sentences of a passage. The first and sixth sentences are given as S1 and S6. The middle four sentences have been jumbled and labelled P, Q, R and S. Find the proper sequence of the four sentences.

S1: The South African Constitution was inaugurated in December 1996.
S6: A special constitutional court enforces the rights enshrined in the Constitution.
P: Its creation and promulgation took place at a time when South Africa still faced the threat of a civil war after the dissolution of the Apartheid Government.
Q: The South African Constitution says that its "Bill of Rights is a cornerstone of democracy in South Africa."
R: Apropos, it forbids discrimination on the grounds of "race, gender, pregnancy, marital status, ethnic or social origin, colour, age, disability, religion, conscience, belief, culture, language and birth".
S: The Bill of Rights grants perhaps the most extensive range of rights to the citizens.
questions.explanation:
P describes the context of its creation; Q introduces the Bill of Rights; S says it grants extensive rights; R gives an example ('Apropos, it forbids discrimination'); S6 names the court that enforces them.
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part A English

questions.question:

Imprest:

An imprest is a fund of money advanced for small, routine expenses (an imprest account).
Answer: (b)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.question:

P: participate in the function
Q: many of the people who had come to
R: the auditorium was over-crowded
S: could not find a seat because

Many of the people who had come to (Q) participate in the function (P) could not find a seat because (S) the auditorium was over-crowded (R).
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part A English

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.question:
Directions: The parts of the sentence have been jumbled and labelled P, Q, R and S. Select the option that sequences the parts correctly.

P: lay outside her existing life
Q: she knew that the answer
R: somewhere in the back of her mind
S: to her questions about life
questions.explanation:
Somewhere in the back of her mind (R) she knew that the answer (Q) to her questions about life (S) lay outside her existing life (P).
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part A English

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.question:
Directions: The parts of the sentence have been jumbled and labelled P, Q, R and S. Select the option that sequences the parts correctly.

P: works of literature
Q: inside the pages of all good
R: lies the truth about some of
S: the more challenging questions posed by humanity
questions.explanation:
Inside the pages of all good (Q) works of literature (P) lies the truth about some of (R) the more challenging questions posed by humanity (S).
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part A English

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.question:
Directions: The parts of the sentence have been jumbled and labelled P, Q, R and S. Select the option that sequences the parts correctly.

P: takes on account of its economic successes
Q: to address continuing social inequality
R: for every stride of progress any nation
S: it takes two back if it is unable
questions.explanation:
For every stride of progress any nation (R) takes on account of its economic successes (P), it takes two back if it is unable (S) to address continuing social inequality (Q).
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part A English

questions.question:
Directions: The parts of the sentence have been jumbled and labelled P, Q, R and S. Select the option that sequences the parts correctly.

P: the book-value of a loan or
Q: an intangible asset over a set period of time
R: used to periodically lower
S: amortisation is an accounting technique
questions.explanation:
Amortisation is an accounting technique (S) used to periodically lower (R) the book-value of a loan or (P) an intangible asset over a set period of time (Q).
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part A English

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: The sentence has a blank space followed by four options. Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

There is more than __________ to get the job done.
questions.explanation:
'More than one way' is idiomatic; 'one' takes a singular noun.
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part A English

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: The sentence has a blank space followed by four options. Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The class decided to organise __________.
questions.explanation:
A singular countable noun mentioned for the first time takes 'a'.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part A English

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: The sentence has a blank space followed by four options. Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The accused __________ before the judge.
questions.explanation:
'To stand trial' is the fixed expression for being tried in court.
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part A English

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: The sentence has a blank space followed by four options. Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The manner in which the demolitions have been carried out __________ scrutiny by the High Court.
questions.explanation:
The subject 'the manner' is singular and the sentence is in the present ('have been carried out'), so 'is under scrutiny'.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part A English

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: The sentence has a blank space followed by four options. Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

I __________ consider the opinions of all stakeholders before taking a final decision.
questions.explanation:
The sentence expresses a commitment about the future; 'will consider' fits. 'Will not' contradicts the sense and 'have' needs 'considered'. ('Shall' is also possible in formal British usage.)
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part A English

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following main industry/industries was/were developed in the second industrial revolution that took place after about 1850?
questions.explanation:
The first industrial revolution was built on cotton, coal, iron and steam. The second (after about 1850) brought chemicals, electricity, steel and later oil and automobiles.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which among the following materials was used in making the Harappan seals?
questions.explanation:
Most Harappan seals were carved from steatite (soapstone).
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which one among the following mahajanapadas in ancient India was an oligarchy?
questions.explanation:
The Vajji confederacy (with Vaishali) was a gana-sangha ruled by an assembly. Kosala, Gandhara and Magadha were monarchies.
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which one of the following sculptures found at Sanchi Stupa is NOT directly inspired by Buddhist ideas?
questions.explanation:
The empty seat, tree and wheel are symbols of the Buddha's meditation, enlightenment and first sermon. The shalabhanjika (woman under a tree) is an auspicious folk fertility motif, not a Buddhist idea.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: History
questions.question: In British India, which one among the following Acts permitted detention without trial for up to two years?
questions.explanation:
The Rowlatt Act (1919) allowed political prisoners to be detained without trial for up to two years.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which one of the following statements about the Bhoodan Movement is correct?
questions.opt_a: The target was to get one-sixth of cultivable land in India as donation
questions.opt_b: It was approved through a Central Government Act
questions.opt_c: It was ensured that the donated land was free from all litigation
questions.opt_d: The first donation of land was in Bihar
questions.explanation:
Vinoba Bhave asked landowners to give one-sixth of their land and set a target of 50 million acres, about one-sixth of India's cultivable land. The first gift was at Pochampally (Telangana) in 1951. There was no central Act, and much donated land was disputed or unfit.
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: The Constitution (Seventy-third Amendment) Act provides for
questions.opt_a: an elaborate system of establishing municipal self-government
questions.opt_b: an elaborate system of establishing panchayats as units of self-government
questions.opt_c: establishing a Commission for Linguistic Minorities
questions.opt_d: the creation of the Jharkhand State
questions.explanation:
The 73rd Amendment (1992) added Part IX on panchayats; the 74th deals with municipalities.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: BHARATPOL portal has been developed by
questions.opt_d: The Securities and Exchange Board of India
questions.explanation:
BHARATPOL, launched in January 2025, was developed by the CBI to connect Indian law enforcement agencies with Interpol for faster international assistance.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which one of the following statements about the Parliament of India is correct?
questions.opt_a: A majority of members of Rajya Sabha are elected by a system of proportional representation by means of single transferable vote
questions.opt_b: The Deputy Chairperson of the Rajya Sabha is nominated by the President from among the members of the Rajya Sabha
questions.opt_c: The Lok Sabha cannot be dissolved before the completion of its five year term
questions.opt_d: The members of Lok Sabha also vote in the election of the members of Rajya Sabha
questions.explanation:
Elected Rajya Sabha members (all but 12) are chosen by state legislators by proportional representation through the single transferable vote. The Deputy Chairman is elected by the House, the Lok Sabha can be dissolved early, and Lok Sabha members do not vote in Rajya Sabha elections.
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.question: Which one among the following does NOT figure among the Five Principles of Panchsheel?
questions.opt_a: Mutual respect for each other's territorial integrity and sovereignty
questions.explanation:
Panchsheel (1954): mutual respect for territorial integrity and sovereignty, non-aggression, non-interference, equality and mutual benefit, and peaceful coexistence.
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Maize (makka) was introduced into India in the seventeenth century via
questions.explanation:
NCERT (Themes in Indian History II) says maize reached India via Africa and Spain and by the seventeenth century was one of the main crops of western India.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

Fifth: Garibi Hatao; Seventh: Food, Work and Productivity; Ninth: Growth with Social Justice and Equality; Eleventh: Faster and More Inclusive Growth.
Answer: (b)

questions.subject: History
questions.question:
Which of the following statements about Srimanta Shankardeva is/are correct?

1. In the late fifteenth century Shankardeva emerged as one of the leading proponents of Vaishnavism in Assam
2. He was the founder of Gaudiya Vaishnavism
3. His teachings are known as Bhagavati Dharma
4. He encouraged the establishment of satra and naam ghar

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Shankardeva led Vaishnavism in Assam from the late 15th century; his teachings are called Bhagavati dharma; he set up satras and naam ghars. Gaudiya Vaishnavism was founded by Chaitanya.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: History
questions.question: At which one among the following places did the British East India Company found its factory in the year 1611?
questions.explanation:
The English set up their first factory on the east coast at Masulipatnam in 1611 (Surat followed in 1613).
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: History
questions.question:
Chronologically arrange the following political events related to Indian National Movement beginning from the earliest:

1. Formation of Swaraj Party
2. Communal Award
3. Lucknow Pact
4. Simla Conference

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Lucknow Pact (1916), Swaraj Party (1923), Communal Award (1932), Simla Conference (1945).
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which among the following Acts provided for the establishment of a Supreme Court of Justice at Calcutta for Europeans, their employees and the citizens of India?
questions.explanation:
The Regulating Act, 1773 set up the Supreme Court at Calcutta (established 1774).
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who, among the following, has introduced a resolution in 1882 which is also called the Magna Carta of Local Self-Government in India?
questions.explanation:
Lord Ripon's resolution of 1882 is called the Magna Carta of local self-government.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which one of the following terms is associated with the practice of Sufism?
questions.explanation:
A murid is a disciple of a Sufi master (pir/shaikh). Jizya is a tax, ijma is consensus in Islamic law and muqaddam a village headman.
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question:
Consider the following features:

1. Consent of the governed
2. Political equality
3. Accountability of the ruled to the ruler

Which of the above feature/features outline democratic rule?
questions.explanation:
Democracy rests on the consent of the governed and political equality. It is the rulers who are accountable to the ruled, not the reverse.
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question:
Placing the earliest first, arrange the following countries in the chronological order in which they granted universal adult franchise:

1. USA
2. Sri Lanka
3. Japan
4. India

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Following NCERT's table: Sri Lanka 1931, Japan 1945, India 1950 and the USA 1965 (when voting rights were secured for all).
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct?
questions.opt_a: The molecules of soap are sodium or potassium salts of long chain fatty acids
questions.opt_b: The molecules of soap contain both hydrophobic and hydrophilic ends
questions.opt_c: Detergents are more effective than soaps in hard water
questions.opt_d: In micelles the ionic-end of the molecules is towards oil droplet while the other end faces outside
questions.explanation:
In a micelle the hydrocarbon (hydrophobic) tails point into the oil droplet and the ionic heads face the water outside.
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements is correct?
questions.opt_a: A neutron is formed by combination of an electron and a proton. Therefore, it is neutral
questions.opt_b: The mass of an electron is about 1/2000 times that of a proton
questions.opt_c: An isotope of cobalt is used in the treatment of goiter
questions.opt_d: J. J. Thomson proposed that the nucleus of an atom contains only neutrons
questions.explanation:
An electron's mass is about 1/1836 (roughly 1/2000) of a proton's. A neutron is a separate particle, iodine-131 treats goitre, and Thomson had no nucleus in his model.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Which one of the following particles in the nucleus of an atom was discovered by J. Chadwick?
questions.explanation:
James Chadwick discovered the neutron in 1932.
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Which one of the following findings is NOT observed in Rutherford's Nuclear Model of Atom?
questions.opt_a: There is a neutral centre in an atom called nucleus
questions.opt_b: Nearly all the mass of an atom resides in the nucleus
questions.opt_c: The electrons revolve around the nucleus in a circular path
questions.opt_d: The size of a nucleus is very small as compared to the size of atom
questions.explanation:
Rutherford found a positively charged centre, not a neutral one.
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Element X forms a chloride with the formula XCl$_2$, which is a solid with high melting point. X would most likely be in the same group of periodic table as
questions.explanation:
XCl$_2$ means valency 2, and the high melting point shows an ionic chloride, like the group 2 metal magnesium (MgCl$_2$).
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.subtopic: Acids, Bases, pH & Commercial Inorganic Salts
questions.question: Which one of the following oxides is a neutral oxide?
questions.explanation:
Carbon monoxide is neutral. CO$_2$ is acidic; Na$_2$O and MgO are basic.
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Which one of the following is also known as Dry ice in its solid form?
questions.explanation:
Solid carbon dioxide is dry ice.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.subtopic: Acids, Bases, pH & Commercial Inorganic Salts
questions.question: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct?
questions.opt_a: A scale measuring hydrogen ion concentration in a solution is called pH scale
questions.opt_b: The higher the hydrogen ion concentration in a solution, higher is its pH
questions.opt_c: We can measure pH generally from 0 to 14 on a pH scale
questions.opt_d: The 'p' in pH stands for 'potenz' in German meaning power
questions.explanation:
pH $=-\log[\mathrm H^+]$, so a higher hydrogen ion concentration means a lower pH.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct?
questions.opt_a: Half mole of nitrogen gas is measured 11.2 litre at STP
questions.opt_b: 17 gram of ammonia gas contains $6.022\times10^{23}$ molecules at STP
questions.opt_c: 22.4 litre of CO$_2$ gas at STP contains 44 gram of molecules
questions.opt_d: 4 gram of hydrogen gas contains $6.022\times10^{23}$ molecules
questions.explanation:
4 g of H$_2$ is 2 mol, i.e. $1.204\times10^{24}$ molecules. The other statements are correct.
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements about a compound is NOT correct?
questions.opt_a: A compound is a substance composed of two or more elements, chemically combined in a fixed proportion
questions.opt_b: Properties of a compound are different from its constituent elements
questions.opt_c: A compound is an impure substance
questions.opt_d: The constituents of a compound can be separated only by chemical or electrochemical reactions
questions.explanation:
A compound is a pure substance with a fixed composition.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.question: Which one of the following nitrogen oxides may dimerize?
questions.explanation:
NO$_2$ has an unpaired electron and dimerises to N$_2$O$_4$.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements regarding oxidation and reduction reactions is NOT correct?
questions.opt_a: If a substance loses hydrogen during reaction, it is reduced
questions.opt_b: If a substance loses oxygen during reaction, it is reduced
questions.opt_c: If a substance gains hydrogen during reaction, it is reduced
questions.opt_d: If a substance gains oxygen during reaction, it is oxidized

Loss of hydrogen is oxidation, not reduction.
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

Normal rain is slightly acidic (about 5.6) from dissolved CO$_2$; rain below pH 5.6 is called acid rain.
Answer: (c)

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Consider the following lines of Longitude and Latitude:

1. Prime Meridian
2. Tropic of Cancer
3. Equator

Which of the above lines is/are a Great Circle?
questions.explanation:
The equator is a great circle. The Prime Meridian with its opposite meridian (180°) forms a great circle, so it is treated as one. The Tropic of Cancer is a small circle.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Which of the following is the correct ascending order of the given minerals in terms of their presence in the Earth's crust?

2. Mica
3. Pyroxene

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Approximate crustal shares: mica about 4-5%, amphiboles about 5-7%, pyroxenes about 11%. Ascending: mica, amphibole, pyroxene.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Which of the following is/are the applied forces in mechanical weathering process?

1. Gravitational force
2. Expansion force
3. Force due to water pressure

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
NCERT: in mechanical weathering the applied forces can be gravitational (overburden, load, shearing), expansion (temperature change, crystal growth, animals) and water pressure from wetting and drying.
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Which of the following is/are cold ocean current/currents?

1. Alaska Current
2. North Atlantic Drift
3. West Wind Drift

Select the answer using the code given below:

The Alaska Current and North Atlantic Drift are warm; the West Wind Drift (Antarctic Circumpolar Current) is cold.
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Geography
questions.theme: Sun angle at the June solstice
questions.question: Which one of the following latitudes will experience a minimum angle of the Sun's rays when it is Summer Solstice in the Northern Hemisphere?
questions.explanation:
On 21 June the Sun is overhead at 23.5°N. Noon altitude is 90° minus the angular distance from 23.5°N: Tropic of Cancer 90°, Equator 66.5°, Arctic Circle 47°, Tropic of Capricorn 43°. The lowest angle is at the Tropic of Capricorn.
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Which of the following statements with reference to Coriolis force is/are correct?

1. Coriolis force acts perpendicular to the pressure gradient force
2. At the equator, the Coriolis force is zero and the wind blows perpendicular to the isobars

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Both are NCERT statements: the Coriolis force acts perpendicular to the pressure gradient force, and at the equator it is zero, so wind blows perpendicular to the isobars.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA I 2025 General Ability Test set A (AEBC-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Which of the following statements with reference to Sleet is/are correct?

1. Sleet is frozen raindrops and refrozen melted snow-water
